significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that benign fine-tuning weakens refusal by perturbing "the parameters supporting the refusal direction" and that preserving its projection behavior causally retains safety; this is a form-(ii) mechanism-plus-intervention claim, not a form-(iii) law, and it chiefly constrains one behavior: refusal-based harmful-compliance. The phenomenon of safety loss under benign fine-tuning is documented by Qi et al., "Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!" (ICLR 2024), while Arditi et al., "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction" (NeurIPS 2024), makes the claimed mechanistic target consequential: the finding would connect that target causally to alignment durability rather than merely show decodability. A negative result would usefully rule out preservation of the compact refusal subspace as sufficient protection and favor more distributed or changing mechanisms, although it would not resolve non-refusal safety behaviors; true and false are therefore distinguishable and informative. The topic-substitution check lowers the assessment from what generic LLM-safety importance might suggest: deleting the specific subspace-preservation mechanism leaves only the broad safety topic, which would not earn this score, while the remaining claim is somewhat sharper than the topic's obvious first hypothesis but still follows the standard separable-mechanism-and-repair template.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is a training-time "regularizer ... that penalizes changes to the model's refusal-direction computation," preserving "its projection behavior on a small safety anchor set"; this is an ex-ante intervention because it acts during customization before post-fine-tuning harmful compliance occurs. It could therefore be used by practitioners who fine-tune or ship aligned models, not only by interpretability researchers, and the hypothesis asserts applicability across benign instruction tuning and domain adaptation while explicitly limiting itself because it "may not generalize to non-refusal safety behaviors" and adversarial fine-tuning can defeat it. After moving to another model, the refusal subspace and supporting parameters would have to be re-extracted, and the conclusion supplies a strategy for looking and regularizing rather than a quantitative relation that predicts the new model's values. The topic-substitution check passes: generic mechanism-based LLM safety supplies no comparable handle or lead time, whereas this specific preventive regularizer does, supporting reach above the topic median but not the transfer-oriented 9–10 band.
